timeTaken.note: Time to build this flow from nothing: from the request to a reviewed suite, including the fix the review asked for and a re-check on all three browsers.

steps.step: Intake and first look, including your answer about folders and accounts
Website explorer: trying the login flow
Requirement analyst: scope, assumptions and risks
Test case designer: writing the test cases and the workbook
Waiting for approval of the test cases
Test architect: planning the page objects
Test writer: writing the test code
Waiting for confirmation of the run
Test runner: 12 tests on three browsers (all passed)
Quality reviewer: found one check that could print the user name

scenarios.journey: A user logs in with the saved test account and sees their Profile page
scenarios.preconditions: Not signed in; the saved test account for this browser is available
scenarios.testData: Saved test account for this browser (user name and password)
steps: Type the saved user name in the "UserName" box
Type the saved password in the "Password" box
scenarios.expected: The Profile page opens. Next to "User Name :" it shows the user name of the saved account, and a "Logout" button is shown.
scenarios.risk: If logging in fails, a user cannot reach their profile or their books

scenarios.feature: Book list and search while signed in
scenarios.journey: A signed-in user opens the Book Store, searches for a book and then clears the search
scenarios.preconditions: Signed in with the saved test account for this browser
scenarios.testData: Saved test account for this browser; search word "Git"
steps: Wait for the books to appear
Type "Git" in the "Type to search" box
scenarios.expected: 8 books are listed. Next to "User Name :" the page shows the user name of the saved account, and a "Log out" button is shown instead of "Login". With "Git", only "Git Pocket Guide" is listed. After clearing the box, all 8 books are listed again.
scenarios.risk: If the list or search is wrong while signed in, a user cannot find a book

scenarios.journey: A signed-in user logs out from the Book Store
scenarios.preconditions: Signed in with the saved test account for this browser; the Book Store is open
scenarios.testData: Saved test account for this browser
steps: Click "Log out" on the Book Store
scenarios.expected: The Login page opens with the "Login" button and an empty "UserName" box. The Book Store then shows the "Login" button again, no "Log out" button and no user name.
scenarios.risk: If logging out does not work, the next person on the same computer could use the account

scenarios.journey: A signed-in user logs out from the Profile page
scenarios.preconditions: Signed in with the saved test account for this browser; the Profile page is open
scenarios.testData: Saved test account for this browser
scenarios.expected: The Login page opens with the "Login" button. The Profile page then shows no user name and reads: "Currently you are not logged into the Book Store application, please visit the login page to enter or register page to register yourself."
scenarios.risk: If logging out from the profile does not work, the account stays open

testData.notes: One saved account per browser (user name and password); values are never written down or shown

risks.description: Shared public practice site: its content and availability can change without notice.
risks.mitigation: Check a few known titles; rerun before reporting a failure.

risks.description: If two browsers used the same account at once, they could sign each other out.
risks.mitigation: Use one saved account per browser (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).

risks.description: The site loads slowly and shows adverts.
risks.mitigation: Wait for page content to show, never for a fixed time.

risks.description: Account details could leak into test names, logs, screenshots or reports.
risks.mitigation: Never print the account details; check the user name only as a match with the saved account.

risks.description: The login boxes are not linked to their labels.
risks.mitigation: Find the boxes by their hints "UserName" and "Password".

risks.description: Firefox and WebKit behave the same as Chromium; only Chromium was explored.
risks.mitigation: Any difference shows up on the first run on all three browsers.

risks.description: The 8 books and the search result for "Git" stay as seen during exploration.
risks.mitigation: Check the number of books and the known title "Git Pocket Guide".

risks.description: The two log-out buttons have different names: "Log out" on the Book Store and "Logout" on the Profile page. It is not stated whether both should be checked.
risks.mitigation: Check the Book Store one as High (the requested flow) and the Profile one as Medium.

risks.description: After logging out, the Profile page does not send the visitor to the Login page; it shows a notice instead. It is not stated which is wanted.
risks.mitigation: Check the notice as seen during exploration; ask whether a move to the Login page is wanted.

risks.description: Not stated: how long a sign-in lasts, whether it survives a reload, and what Back shows after logging out. Wrong-login messages were not seen.
risks.mitigation: Not covered by these test cases; ask if they are wanted.

risks.description: On the test laptop, reading the saved account details from the credentials file (inside the OneDrive-synced folder) sometimes stalled for more than 30 seconds, so a Firefox test timed out before it started. It passed when run again with no code change. This is the laptop, not the website or the test.
risks.mitigation: Keep the credentials file out of OneDrive sync, or point CREDENTIALS_FILE to a local copy outside the synced folder.
